# Version Control and Reproducibility

## Overview
Reproducibility, the ability for you or someone else to re-run your analysis and get the same result, is a cornerstone of trustworthy data science, and version control is how you achieve it. Git is a system that tracks changes to your code over time: you 'commit' snapshots with messages, create 'branches' to try ideas without breaking your main work, and 'merge' them back when ready. GitHub hosts your Git repositories online, enabling backup, collaboration, and a public portfolio that employers can see. Reproducibility also requires capturing your environment: listing exact package versions in a requirements.txt and using virtual environments so your project runs the same on any machine. A professional repository has a clear structure (separate folders for data, notebooks, and source code), a README explaining what the project does and how to run it, and a .gitignore that keeps large data files and secrets out of version control. These practices transform a one-off notebook into a shareable, maintainable project, and they're expected in any real data science job.

## Deep Dive
This module covers: Git basics (add, commit, branch, merge); GitHub and remote repositories; Reproducible environments (requirements.txt, virtual envs); Project structure and README files; Notebooks vs scripts and .gitignore. Mastering these ideas is essential because they appear repeatedly in production AI systems.

### What You Will Learn
- The core theory behind today's topic.
- How to apply it using Python, NumPy, Pandas, or the relevant framework.
- How to evaluate results and avoid common mistakes.
- Where to find authoritative references when you need deeper detail.

### Real-World Context
In industry, these skills are used daily: data scientists clean messy survey data, AI engineers deploy models to REST APIs, and automation engineers orchestrate pipelines. Today's practical task simulates one of these real-world scenarios.

## Hands-On Practice
**Practical Task:** Initialize a Git repository for an existing project, make several commits, create and merge a branch, add a requirements.txt and README, and push it all to a new GitHub repository.
**Mini Project:** Take one of your earlier projects and turn it into a professional, reproducible GitHub repository with proper structure, a documented README, pinned dependencies, and a clean commit history.
**Assignment:** Write a README for one of your projects that a stranger could follow to reproduce your results from scratch.

Complete all three sections. Each completed section earns points toward your CalibiAI Score. If you are unsure about any part, use the AI assessment popup to submit your work and receive dynamic feedback from DeepSeek.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
Many beginners rush into coding before fully understanding the data. Others skip validation steps and overestimate model performance. This module helps you build the discipline of checking assumptions first, then applying algorithms systematically.

## Career Impact
The skills covered today are frequently tested in technical interviews and required in entry-level AI engineering roles. Building a portfolio that demonstrates mastery of these concepts will significantly improve your job prospects.

## Key Takeaways
1. Theory guides practice — understand before coding.
2. Clean data and clear metrics are more valuable than complex models.
3. Document your steps for reproducibility.
4. Communication matters: explain results to non-technical stakeholders.
